CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right knee injury with pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient sustained a right knee injury one week ago while at a trampoline park with his wife, which was his first time at such a facility. He was on the trampoline when he heard a snap and experienced immediate pain on the lateral (outside) aspect of the right knee. Since the injury, he has managed it with elevation. He attempted to treat pain with Tylenol without significant relief and has not used ice or heat. The patient reports he can bend and straighten the knee but experiences pain with movement. He can bear weight but notes a slight limp when walking. On physical examination, ecchymosis and edema are noted on the lateral aspect of the right knee with no effusion appreciated. Range of motion is decent despite discomfort. Right knee x-ray was obtained showing no evidence of fracture or bony abnormality.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension
Diabetes mellitus

MEDICATIONS
Lisinopril 20 mg daily (patient reports taking most days)
Metformin 500 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient does not exercise regularly and is inconsistent with exercise regimen. He attended the trampoline park for recreational purposes with his wife and this was his first visit. Patient expresses reluctance about physician visits. Regarding diet, he attempts to monitor intake and is focusing on reducing carbohydrate consumption but is not counting calories or macros. He denies following a specific diet plan or a low sodium diet.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure 180/80 mmHg (elevated)
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmur appreciated
Pulmonary: Lungs clear bilaterally
Right knee: Lateral aspect with tenderness to palpation, ecchymosis, and edema. Medial aspect non-tender. Range of motion intact with decent flexibility. No effusion. Gait with slight limp. Able to bear weight.

RESULTS
Right knee x-ray: No evidence of fracture or bony abnormality.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Right knee pain - Lateral ligament strain
   - Prescribe meloxicam 15 mg daily for pain and swelling
   - Refer to physical therapy to strengthen surrounding muscles and prevent further injury
   - Consider further imaging if pain persists
   - Counsel that this is a common injury that typically heals on its own

2. Hypertension
   - Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily
   - Order echocardiogram
   - Discussed concern that blood pressure is not at target level; may require medication modification based on echo results

3. Diabetes mellitus
   - Order A1C to assess long-term glycemic control
   - Order lipid panel for potential medication adjustments if needed
